newsitem.title: INDIA: India to detail energy projects by year-end.
newsitem.headline: India to detail energy projects by year-end.

text.p: India will reveal by the end of the year details of its investment plans for energy projects, junior Power Minister Yogendra Alagh said on Wednesday.

Alagh told reporters in the Indian capital after addressing a seminar on sustainable development that the details would figure in the final document of India's ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002), expected to be released in December.
"The ninth Plan will have details on private and public investment and the whole question of public and private linkages," he said.
The document will also clearly spell out the government's policy on the use of fuels like coal and natural gas in electricity generation, Alagh said.
India is courting private investment to set up power plants under a six-year-old economic reform programme.

Alagh said the government, which approved the setting up of regulatory bodies for electricity on Tuesday, will introduce a bill to help create federal and state-level regulators in the current monsoon session of the parliament.
The regulatory bodies, which will fix power tariffs, are considered a prelude to a regime of market-based electricity prices in India.
Experts say power charges artificially controlled by the state need to be raised if India is to attract foreign investment in the power sector.
The government also plans to introduce an Energy Efficiency Bill which, if approved, would help conserve energy resources, Alagh said.
